# Finding the Indefinite Integral ∫ -2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Setting Up the Problem

I need to compute: ∫ -2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = -2 ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Computing ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx via Integration by Parts

**First application** (u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)dx):

∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx = exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx

**Second application** on ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx (u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)dx):

∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Solving the Equation

Substituting back:

∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

2*∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)

∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx = exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x))/2

## Applying the Constant Factor

∫ -2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = -2 * [exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x))/2] = -exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*cos(x) + C

## Verification

d/dx[-exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*cos(x)]
= -[exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)] - [exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*sin(x)]
= -exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)
= -2*exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

<answer>-exp(x)*sin(x) - exp(x)*cos(x) + C</answer>
